notes: The parts list is unchanged. The only remaining check finding is that hub1 (Google Nest Hub Max) has no connection. It is not a real problem for this manual, so hub1 stays.

The tutorial's parts list names the Nest Hub Max as the Thread Border Router. It reaches the Nano Matter only over the wireless Thread/Matter network, and the manual describes no cable, mount or physical contact between them. A joined, contact, blocks or electrical edge would record a connection that does not exist.
The spec says to use exactly the parts the tutorial lists, so I kept the hub rather than drop it to satisfy the check.
The socket has two kinds of port: wire-end pigtails 1 and 2 on the mains side, and lead contacts B1 and B2 for the bulb. Inside the socket B1 is conducted to 1 and B2 to 2.

AC path: cable live (L) goes to relay COM. Relay NO goes to socket pigtail 1, through the bulb, and back via socket pigtail 2 to the cable neutral (N). When the relay is open the circuit is broken, as the tutorial says.
The wiring diagram image was not available, so the wiring follows the text. The relay is powered from 3V3 and GND and driven from D4.

Nano Matter breadboard placement is assumed. It sits across the centre gap in columns 1-15 with the standard Nano layout: 3V3 at column 2 on the top half, GND at column 4 and D4 at column 7 on the bottom half.
The Grove relay module is reached by three jumper wires, which stand in for the coloured Grove cable in the photo.
The plug end of the AC cable goes to the wall outlet, which is not a part. The far end of the USB-C cable goes to a power source that the tutorial does not list.
The orange wire nut in the photo is not in the parts list, so it is omitted.
